facts.claim: Guo and colleagues (2017) found that modern neural networks, unlike those of a decade earlier, are poorly calibrated, and that temperature scaling, one number fitted on held-out data, is surprisingly effective at fixing it.
Kadavath and colleagues at Anthropic (2022) found that larger language models are well calibrated on diverse multiple-choice and true/false questions.

OpenAI’s GPT-4 report (2023) shows its pre-trained model well calibrated on part of the MMLU test, with an ECE of 0.007, and its post-trained model much less so, at 0.074. OpenAI’s figures, for a far larger model.
Glenn Brier proposed his score in 1950 to check weather forecasts given as probabilities: the average squared gap between each forecast and what happened.
Geifman and El-Yaniv (2017) built selective classifiers on trained deep networks: you set the error rate you can accept, and the classifier declines the inputs it must to keep it.
